messages:
alex (support): FYI customer AcroMetrics just opened an escalation — their p99 on /v1/generate shot from ~500ms to ~2s around 08:15 UTC. They say it started right after we rolled a batcher tweak. They included a repro curl and traces. Can SRE triage? :eyes:

maya (oncall): on it. any quick links to grafana / alert?

alex (support): Grafana panel: https://grafana.redwood.net/d/latency/p99-over-time?orgId=1&from=now-3h&to=now . Alert fired at 08:18. Customer trace: https://traces.redwood.net/trace/abcd1234 . Repro curl they used:

```bash
curl -sS -H \"Authorization: Bearer <cust-key>\" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rdx-med","input":"short prompt"}'
```

alex (support): Note: rollout note from deploy-bot shows commit a1b2c3 changed continuous_batcher.max_wait_ms from 6 -> 40ms around 08:05 by eng-runtime.

deploy-bot: rollout a1b2c3 -> prod-started (canary 10%)

deploy-bot: rollout a1b2c3 -> prod-complete (5m)

maya (oncall): ok i see matching spike in p95/p99 on prod-us-west-2. p50 unchanged. That screams tail-head blocking in batching. Can we grab batch size distribution and per-worker qlen? josh, li, ping.

josh (eng-sre): pulling logs. here's batch-size histogram from the last 30m (aggregated):
```
0 tokens: 12%
1-8 tokens: 44%
9-64 tokens: 38%
>64: 6%
mean batch size: 7.2
mean wait: 28ms
timeouts hit: 18% of requests hit max_wait
```

josh (eng-sre): interesting: many tiny batches but lots of timeouts hitting the new 40ms wait, then some workers assemble very large batches (~120 seq len) leading to long device compute that blocks later requests. head-of-line.

li (perf): that matches. continuous-batcher change increased max_wait to 40ms so it waits longer to fill batches. For our token distribution small requests were fine before because we favored tiny-batcher when wait was 6ms. Now mixed workload causes more timeouts and larger occasional batches that inflates tail. Also kv-cache miss rate slightly higher at same time (maybe unrelated).

tracy (customer-success): customer says their users see intermittent 1-2s delays, primarily on short prompts. They're pretty unhappy.

alex (support): customer asked for ETA. we should propose rollback or mitigation ASAP.

maya (oncall): mitigation plan: (1) revert continuous_batcher.max_wait to 6ms for prod-us-west-2; (2) enable per-model tiny-batcher override for their model; (3) rollout canary for 10% then 100%. Are we able to hotpatch config?

josh (eng-sre): we can hotpatch config via config-service. I can apply a canary to reduce max_wait to 10ms first (less risky) and watch. If p99 improves, we either keep 10ms or revert to 6ms. I'll run the canary now.

infra-bot: config-change request: {service: continuous-batcher, region: us-west-2, key: max_wait_ms, from: 40, to: 10, author: josh} queued.

deploy-bot: canary config applied to 10% of traffic (tag: canary/max_wait-10ms).

josh (eng-sre): canary metrics: after 2m p99 on canary group down from 2.0s -> 540ms. overall prod p99 down by ~20%. still some tail in non-canary.

maya (oncall): good signal. let's promote to 100% in 5min unless it regresses. any risks? li?

li (perf): risk: slightly higher compute overhead due to more tiny batches (cost up ~3-5%), but latency wins. Also need to watch GPU utilization and token-per-second — might drop; autoscaler should handle short term. KV-cache miss should not be impacted by wait directly.

josh (eng-sre): promoting to 100% now.

deploy-bot: config-change promoted to 100% (max_wait_ms=10)

maya (oncall): metrics 5m after promote: p99 baseline ~560ms, p95 ~220ms. Customer acked reduced delays in slack. I'll message them. :thumbsup:

alex (support): customer confirmed improvement in thread and asked for RCA and permanent fix.

li (perf): RCA draft notes: root cause — config change increasing continuous_batcher.max_wait_ms from 6->40ms made the batcher wait longer to coalesce requests. With our mix of very short prompts and occasional long sequences, this caused two effects: (1) more requests hit timeout boundary causing a bimodal batch size distribution; (2) occasional large batches produced long GPU compute times, causing head-of-line blocking and p99 spikes. Secondary contributor: certain models lack per-model tiny-batcher overrides so the global wait applied everywhere.

josh (eng-sre): reproduction steps for CI/debug:
```
# simulate mixed workload: many short requests + infrequent long ones
python tools/sim_batcher_load.py --short-rate 90 --long-rate 10 --short-seq 8 --long-seq 300 --duration 3m --batcher-wait-ms 40
# watch p99
```

josh (eng-sre): logs from the worker showing timeouts:
```
[2026-03-15T08:12:34Z] batcher: waited 40ms, emitting batch size 3 (timeout)
[2026-03-15T08:12:34Z] worker: submit batch len 3 -> queuing gpu compute (est 6ms)
[2026-03-15T08:12:34Z] batcher: waited 40ms, emitting batch size 120 (filled)
[2026-03-15T08:12:34Z] worker: submit batch len 120 -> compute 1600ms
[2026-03-15T08:12:34Z] request: observed latency 1870ms
```

maya (oncall): good logs. followups:
- revert default to 6ms for continuous-batcher in prod globally unless explicitly overridden per-model
- add a safety guard: if p99 increases by >30% within 10min after config change, auto rollback config to previous value
- add per-model tiny-batcher boolean and default it ON for short-prompt models
- alert on high fraction of timeout-emitted batches (>10%)

li (perf): I'll file a perf-ticket to add guardrail and per-model override + cost/runbook tradeoffs. Estimated 3 dev-days.

tracy (customer-success): I'll send AcroMetrics a summary and timeline and offer them a week of higher SLA credits.

alex (support): thanks all. I'll close the escalation after we PR the RCA and postmortem. Customer's slack message: \"Thanks, noticed big improvement — hoping for a writeup.\"

maya (oncall): recording incident: INC-2026-0315-02. Linking to playbooks: https://wiki.redwood.ai/playbooks/batcher-tail-latency

josh (eng-sre): PR raised to revert default in config-service: https://git.redwood.ai/repo/infra/commit/a1b2c3-revert-batcher-default . Also added canary flagging change and a tiny-batcher opt-in flag.

infra-bot: opened incident ticket INC-2026-0315-02 and attached logs.

alex (support): any further actions before we close thread?

li (perf): change the alert thresholds for p99-on-prod to include correlated increase in batch-timeout rate. I'll update dashboards and add the guard ticket to sprint.

maya (oncall): closing loop: 08:05 config change -> 08:15 customer sees p99 spike -> 08:20 canary -> 08:25 promote -> 08:30 reduction confirmed -> RCA + PR + followups assigned. Good job.

alex (support): thanks team. will paste RCA to customer and postmortem to #postmortems later. :sparkles:
